The cases of a linear dipole and a circular loop antenna excited by a delta-gap source are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The butterfly: a broadband, aerodynamic antenna for airborne missile scoring using impulse radar
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A description is given of the butterfly antenna which provides an aerodynamic replacement for the resistively loaded cone, for use with an airborne impulse radar. The missile-sensing system is described, and antenna requirements and developments are discussed. Results of measured performance are presented. The butterfly antenna is shown to give a clean pulse, although the pulse radiated sideways does have significant overshoot. The elevation pattern is broader and the efficiency is slightly higher than that in cones previously used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some results of the scattering of simple conducting bodies in the vicinity of a cloud of dipoles
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A method-of-moments wire model is employed to obtain the variation of the radar cross section of a perfectly conducting plate when it is placed near a cloud of resonant dipoles. The effect of the relative position between the plate and the cloud is studied. Different cases of coupling between the dipoles are also analyzed in order to study their influence on the interaction between the plate and the cloud. A time-domain response is obtained when a RF pulse is incident on a plate hidden by a cloud of dipoles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: S-band diplexing radiating element design
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The details of a diplexing antenna design are presented. The device principle is given, and the loss budget is reduced by choosing the frequency bandwidth of the radiators. It is shown that, when designing a diplexing antenna for close reception/transmission bands, the antenna voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) has an indirect impact on the loss budget. Multipole antennas are well suited to achieve an efficient diplexing device, but their design must include all interactions between components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diffraction of H-polarized Hermite-Gaussian beams from a sinusoidal conducting surface
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The H-polarized case is treated for the diffraction of Hermite-Gaussian beams from a sinusoidal conducting grating. The analytical solutions of plane-wave diffraction from sinusoidal gratings have been given previously for E- and H-polarized cases (Kojima, 1990). The incident beam-wave can be expressed by the plane-wave spectrum representation, and for the incidence of each plane wave component the space-harmonic solutions of the diffracted field can be found by using the analytical solutions. Therefore, the total diffracted fields are constructed by superposing the space harmonic solutions. The far-zone diffracted field can be evaluated by the saddle point method. The errors of the energy conservation are compared between E- and H-polarizations, and numerical examples of the diffraction pattern are obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systematic design of microstrip arrays at the Ku band
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The author presents systematic design steps leading to the fabrication and testing of practical microstrip arrays operating at the Ku-band. The following specifications are considered: frequency: 15.0 GHz; performance bandwidth: 500 MHz; gain: 13 dB; polarization: right-handed circular; 3 dB beamwidth: approx. 50 degrees ; axial ratio: 1 dB; sidelobe level: better than -10 dB; and disposition: modular subarray configuration. Several four-element arrays have been fabricated and tested. Preliminary results show that by placing one or two layers of filter screens (arrays of suitable patches) the axial ratio performance could be favorably modified and the gain, sidelobe level, and bandwidth could simultaneously be improved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of large-scale surface waves on the radar sea return at low grazing angles
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The influence of anisotropic large-scale surface waves on the temporal-spatial structure of the radar sea echo was investigated experimentally. A shipboard surface search radar with two all-around looking aerials (wavelengths 3 and 10 cm, 25 m height) was used as the source of radio-waves. The influence of azimuthal beam divergence on the structure of the radar signal was analyzed. The statistical processing procedure applied here to the received backscatter gives sufficient information about the anisotropic large-scale wave motion and makes it possible to investigate the fine structure of microwave radar scattering at low grazing angles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An empirical model of TEC over the continent of China
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An empirical model based on Fourier harmonic analysis for calculating ionospheric total electron content (TEC) over Xinxiang, China (35.3 degrees N, 113.9 degrees E), is presented for the period November 1981 to June 1985. The data used are from observation of the radio beacon satellite ETS-2 during the descending half of the solar cycle from 1981 to 1985. The harmonic components and annual coefficients of the TEC are examined. The representative diurnal variations of modeled and observed TEC for four months in the different seasons in Xinxiang are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PO optimized dual-offset reflector antenna with subreflector scan mechanism
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A dual-offset reflector limb sounding antenna is described where the beam scan is provided by a linear displacement of the subreflector. This technique yields the advantage of a very low mass to be moved. The numerical design method which is immediately based on the physical optics (PO) procedure achieves improved scan performance without severe pattern problems by adequately shaping both reflectors. The method involves an evolution strategy optimization algorithm where both the subreflector and main reflector surfaces are characterized in the spatial domain in order to reduce the optimization parameters significantly. The example of a shaped dual-offset 200 GHz elliptical Cassegrain reflector antenna with nearly constant half-power beamwidth as a function of the scan angle demonstrates the efficiency of the design method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic scattering from three-dimensional dielectric objects by field iteration method
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An iteration method is presented for solving electromagnetic scattering of 3D dielectric objects. The convergence, stability, effectiveness, and accuracy of the solution obtained by the method are proved. Radar cross section versus incident angle is plotted for a dielectric plate with 0.813 lambda square by 0.051 lambda thick and epsilon /sub r/=4. The numerical results calculated by using the proposed iteration equation are compared with measurements and with the moment-method solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadband scattering matrix measurements and their modelling
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present measured broadband scattering matrix (SM) data and extend results on the description and modelling of broadband polarimetric data. The SM depends on the transmitted frequency and on the illumination direction of the radar, which is characterized by the directional vector in the target coordinate system. The bandwidth of the measurement data is 8.5 GHz, f/sub o/=18.0 GHz. Several scale model aircraft were measured under monostatic constraints in an anechoic chamber for different directions. The broadband SM variation of different targets at the same aspect angle is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering by double gratings with three layered dielectric slabs
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors have investigated the scattering properties of an electromagnetic wave by a grating whose structure consists of three dielectric slabs and strips on the upper side of the slabs from the viewpoint of a polarization discriminator. In the analysis, they used the spectral domain method combined with the sampling theorem. They have also studied the grating problem whose structure is asymmetrical and double structured with a dielectric slab in the case of oblique incidence. The method is extended to analyze the problem of an asymmetrical double-structured grating backed with three-layered dielectric slabs. The expressions for the scattered field are obtained by means of the superposition of the results of the single grating case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A bandwidth enhancement technique for microstrip fed slot arrays
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A theoretical model that shows that the concept of double-tuned waveguide coupled slots is a feasible approach for increasing bandwidth is developed. A full-wave integral equation technique has been developed which allows the analysis of not only thick slots. but also slots which are coupled through a section of waveguide. The latter case also provides a mechanism for improved performance. By adjusting the slots on the ends of the waveguide section to different lengths. one can essentially 'stagger tune' each slot to a different frequency, increasing the overall bandwidth. Within the limited range of parameter variation used, apparent bandwidth increases in the order of at least 50% have been seen. To illustrate the behavior of the structure, a 0.60 in*0.60 in cavity fed by a stripline with a ground spacing of .125 in at 9.7 GHz is studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering from primary feeds with corrugated soft surfaces-effect on the secondary radiation pattern
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown that for small and medium-sized circular symmetric reflector antennas it is very important to include the effect of the multiple scattering between the feed and the reflector when determining the secondary pattern. In particular, when corrugated soft surfaces are used to improve the polarization characteristics of primary feeds, the corrugations will cause very high cross-polarization due to multiple scattering. This is very well predicted by the multiple scattering approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method of treating vector analysis
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A novel method of treating vector analysis is suggested. By means of this method the three basic functions in vector analysis, namely, the gradient, the divergence and the curl and the integral theorems involving these functions can be derived by a relatively simple and orderly approach. All vector identities can be obtained by an algebraic manipulation without performing the differentiation. The key feature of this work is to introduce an operational expression with a symbolic operator which is more general than the conventional del operator. The rest of the analysis is straightforward.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of a microstrip patch antenna using the method of moments
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An analysis of a microstrip patch antenna on a finite dielectric substrate is presented. The antenna is excited by the feedline passing below the dielectric bed. For analysis purposes, the patch, the feedline, and the dielectric substrate are modeled by triangular patches. A set of coupled integral equations, in terms of equivalent currents, is obtained by using the equivalence principle and associated boundary conditions. The equations are then solved using the method of moments. The numerical results are compared with experimental measurements, exhibiting good agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new calibration algorithm of wideband polarimetric measurement system
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A novel calibration algorithm is developed based on three calibrators: a flat plate, a 0-degree dihedral corner reflector, and a Theta degree dihedral corner reflector. This algorithm has the advantage that the three calibrators are not required at the same range nor with the same radar cross section. The rotation angle theta of the third calibrator can be derived in the reflector. This calibration technique is particularly suitable for the calibration of a polarimetric radar under field conditions as the flat plate is replaced by a trihedral corner reflector.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel beamformer for cancelling jammers by exactly nulling
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A novel beamformer which considers the noise density term in the array covariance matrix is presented. It can create exact zeros in jammer directions regardless of the noise power. Furthermore, the extraneous zeros of its beam pattern are designed far away from the look direction, and they are robust to noise. Simulations showed that the beamformer can reject interference more effectively than other beamformers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction modelling of indoor radio propagation for the pico-cellular environment
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An analytical method for the prediction of power delay profiles within a room environment is presented. The model works directly on a 3D description of a room. This simple geometry-based reflection model for the calculation of delay spread values has been shown to work well with measured results. The maximum and typical delay spreads have been found by both model and measurement to be largely determined by room size: the larger the room the greater the delay spread. The narrowband characteristics have been modeled and found to agree well with the standard theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Guided wave propagation on two-dimensional clusters of directly-coupled cavity resonators
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An attempt is made to determine the guided-wave propagation properties of electrically large, two-dimensional delay structures, composed of clusters of directly coupled, high-Q cavity resonators, ordered in either a square or in a hexagonal lattice. The approach used considers the unit-cells as linear reciprocal multiport networks, exhibiting either C/sub 4V/-symmetry or C/sub 6V/-symmetry, consistent with either the square-lattice or the hexagonal-lattice ordering of the unit cells. The image-transfer-function matrix of a single unit-cell uniquely determines the dispersion characteristics of the delay structure within any given passband; the guided-wave attenuation, a function of frequency, within any given stopband; and the natural port-modes of the unit-cell (defined by the eigenvectors of the image-transfer-function matrix).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A design procedure for synthesising dual-shaped offset reflector antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The various parameters that affect the synthesis of dual-shaped offset reflector antennas are investigated. In addition, a design procedure for selecting appropriate values for the antenna parameters is proposed. This basically consists of assigning one parameter as a reference and then obtaining values for the remaining parameters. The set of parameters that is obtained specifies the optimum values for synthesizing the required dual-shaped offset reflector antenna.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast converging modal analysis of rectangular irises in rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The susceptance of a rectangular iris in a rectangular waveguide is obtained using a mode matching formulation. The slow convergent series and relative convergence that frequently limit the application of the method are avoided by a proper choice of basis functions and series transformations based on the Poisson summation formula. Comparisons of theoretical results with measurements confirm the accuracy of the method over a wide range of frequencies and iris dimensions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An EVA antenna sampling and switching system for space station communication
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The design of an EVA (extravehicular activity) antenna sampling and switching system is presented. The system utilizes four separate antennas for full spherical coverage with a space station. The antennas are placed at optimal locations on the back-pack of the EVA astronaut for best coverage performance. Continuous power-level monitoring of the four antennas results in the selection of the best antenna (the one receiving the highest signal level) for communication purposes. The system consists of four log conical spiral antennas, two single-pole-four-throw PIN diode switches, and a double conversion sampling channel that feeds a peak-level detector. A microcontroller algorithm cycles the sampling and switching of antennas based on the level detector output. Attention is given to the block diagram of the system, the development of in-house components, the control algorithm, and the results of composite antenna pattern testing. Measured composite patterns are compared to a computer-synthesized composite pattern derived from individual antenna patterns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiport network model for two-port gap-coupled rectangular microstrip patches
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A multiport network modeling (MNM) approach is developed for the analysis and design of a gap-coupled two-port rectangular microstrip patch. The case when the radiating edge is along the gap is considered. A good agreement between moment-method results and the results based on the MNM approach has been obtained verifying the accuracy of the MNM approach developed for gap-coupled patch.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from a perfectly conducting strip embedded in a dielectric cylinder
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Scattering from a perfectly conducting strip arbitrarily embedded inside a dielectric cylinder of circular or elliptical cross-section is investigated. Numerical results are obtained, and their accuracy is investigated for a variety of physical and electric parameters by comparing the scattered field pattern with numerical results obtained using other techniques. It is found that the numerical computations based on this analysis are rapidly convergent and few terms are needed to obtain reasonably accurate results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of strong-anisotropic fluctuations of the refractive index on the beyond-the-horizon propagation of SHF
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The author presents a technique for investigating the influence of layered fluctuations of the refractivity on transhorizon radio-wave propagation in an evaporation duct. Numerical calculations show that these fluctuations have a significant influence on the transhorizon propagation. It is found that the mean intensity of the EM field considerably exceeds that in the case of an undisturbed waveguide and decreases along the earth's surface more slowly. The field distribution obeys the logarithmic normal distribution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The experimental determination of the calibrated S-parameters of a single resonant-slot array element
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A simple and quick experimental method has been developed for experimentally determining the calibrated scattering parameters of a single resonant-slot array element. The obtained calibrated scattering matrix is defined at two planar interfaces directly coincident with the front and back surfaces of the metal plate surrounding the slot. This measurement method determines different scattering matrices for the same slot, depending on the type of waveguide and the specific waveguide mode used to feed it. An example of a calibrated transmission response of a single slot, excited by the fundamental TE/sub 11/ mode of the cylindrical cavity used to feed it on either side, is presented. The slot resonance appears to be very wide and there is hardly any transmission-phase lag at its center.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability of scattering formulations with multiple elemental current excitations
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The use of the equivalent incident current as the exciting function has been proven economical and efficient in several applications regarding planar problems. In this formulation, the excitation is expressed in the same language used for the unknown induced current, and is expanded into the same basis functions used for the induced current distribution. The current amplitudes on the scatterer for any elemental pulse-type excitation are referred to as pulse responses. Following their evaluation, the solution for any incident field can be synthesized as a weighted summation of the pulse responses. When the individual pulse responses are computed with a finite error, the combination of the pulse responses gives rise to an accumulated error. A physical model which can explain the course taken by the total error shows that if root-mean-square error is small enough, then the accumulation takes place in an oscillatory manner. The physical model is presented, followed by a numerical study which supports the model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple aperture feed for CP microstrip patch antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors introduce a simple design for producing circularly polarized (CP) radiation from a microstrip patch by the use of the aperture coupling technique. Aperture coupling is advantageous in microwave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC) applications since posts, probes, and vias are not required. In addition, the feed circuitry is isolated from the antenna environment by the ground plane. The present design is simpler than the dual aperture coupled CP patch, but has better performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modal analysis of dielectric loaded coaxial probe fed circular waveguide radiator
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An almost rigorous procedure for analyzing dielectric resonator antennas in cylindrical enclosures is presented. The resonant frequency and radiation pattern of a circular waveguide radiator have been analyzed by the method presented. The primary consideration in this special design has been the bandwidth. Experimental results and theoretical predictions for two cases ( in =4,12) are shown. As is evident from this comparison, the method has a reasonable accuracy. In both cases, a piecewise sinusoidal distribution for the probe current has been assumed. In general a limited number of modes in both inhomogeneous and homogeneous regions provides sufficiently accurate results for many practical cases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of rectangular anisotropic dielectric waveguide structures
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The finite-difference method is used in the analysis of rectangular anisotropic waveguide structures. A formulation that was first applied to isotropic dielectric channels diffused into an isotropic dielectric is extended to include anisotropic dielectric channels and anisotropic substrates. This formulation makes it possible to analyze not only the step index of refraction profiles but also arbitrarily varying index profiles. Examples of practical interest are shown, and the results are compared with those obtained from other methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of array patterns with deep nulls by use of one couple phases
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A method of forming a pattern with a deep null by a couple of phases is proposed. The proposed method yields a pattern with a null at a prescribed direction by modifying phases of elements. It has been found that, in order to steer the nulls or deep nulls, it is necessary to adjust a couple of phases. It is pointed out that the pattern modified by a couple of phases cannot form deep nulls in some directions. In that case, the pattern with deep nulls can be steered by adjusting more couples of phases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Limitations of a sidelobe canceller concept
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An analysis is presented which suggests that adding a sidelobe canceller to an existing antenna will not produce effective cancellation over a bandwidth. fortunately, an alternative exists which uses adaptive transversal filters to correct for antenna dispersion and a simple set of horn elements whose gain exceeds the sidelobe gain of the main reflector to avoid unnecessary increases in the system noise temperature. The horn elements also avoid any gain loss due to increased aperture blockage from the additional auxiliary feeds in the focal region.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Near-field investigations to determine the lines of constant phased for an airborne position-finding antenna-system
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A method is presented which makes it possible to calculate the scattered field very close to the surface of a perfectly conducting body as well as the surface itself. The method is based on the representation of the scattered field by an integral over the surface current distribution. The integrand is treated by identical transformations in such a way that the singular terms can be integrated analytically, while the remaining nonsingular terms are integrated numerically. The surface current distribution is determined by the magnetic field integral equation. The theory is validated by experiments by means of the scattered field of a metallic cube with an edge length of a wavelength. The normal and tangential electric near-field of the cube is measured by small probes, and the results are compared with those of the theory. The theoretical results of the near-field distribution of a cube and an airplane are presented using lines of constant phase.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of shunt slots in the narrow wall of X band waveguide using simple formulas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Design formulas for the normalized conductance of inclined slots in the narrow wall of an X-band waveguide are given. The formulas are derived using binomial regression of the experimental data given by E.W. Guptill and W. H. Watson (1949). The formulas are simple and accurate enough for the practical design of the shunt slot in the narrow wall of the waveguide. The simple formula obtained here can be used in the design of a slotted waveguide array at 9.375 GHz. The good agreement of numerical results obtained with the experimental data shows that this formula can be used over a wide range of inclination angles of slots and still obtain the accurate conductance values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cylindrical-rectangular microstrip antenna with the patch along a helical direction
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The cavity model with magnetic side walls and dyadic Green's functions is used for the analysis of a cylindrical-rectangular microstrip antenna with the patch along a helical direction. The input impedance and the radiation pattern are calculated for the antenna operating in the TM/sub 01/ mode. The expressions obtained for the resonant frequency and the input impedance with the patch along a pitch angle are identical to those obtained by K.M. Luk et al. (1989) when the patch is along the axial direction. As expected, the radiation pattern depends on the pitch angle and on the substrate dielectric permittivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple target direction finding and intercept using small aperture antenna arrays
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The author addresses the problem of cochannel radio signal interference which inhibits direction finding (DF) and accurate demodulation. An approach has been developed, using eigenanalysis and adaptive array techniques, for calculating two-dimensional lines-of-bearing on multiple incoherent signals incident on an eight-element circularly disposed, small aperture antenna array and for allowing copy of each of the signals. The direction-finding approach is based upon R.O. Schmidt's (1981) MUSIC algorithm and the copy algorithm is based upon a signal subtraction method, which utilizes eigenvalue and eigenvector data. A numerical simulation of both the DF and copy approaches was performed to evaluate their performance in multiple scenarios.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rough elevated layers and tropospheric microwave propagation
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A theoretical approach is described which takes into account the roughness of the tropospheric layers in line-of-sight microwave links. The approach used here is essentially that used by A. R. Webster (1983). where the elevated layer is modeled using an arctan function to describe the variation in refractivity N, with height, h, In order to simulate the variation of the layer height along the path a collection of sinusoids is used with varying amplitude, wavelength and phase, so that the layer height, h/sub o/, is modified in a specified way: being differentiable, this choice allows the gradient Delta N to be determined readily despite the horizontal gradients introduced by the fluctuations. Results are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering solution from a large 2-D inhomogeneous scatterer by a fast recursive algorithm
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A fast recursive algorithm has been applied to solve the scattering solution of a large 2D inhomogeneous body for TM (transverse magnetic) waves. The inhomogeneous body is first divided into N subscatterers. The algorithm uses an aggregate T matrix and translation formulas for the solution of n+1 subscatterers from the solution for n subscatterers. The computational complexity of the algorithms is of O(NMP/sup 2/), where NM is the number of unknowns and P is the number of harmonics required in the translation formulas. The memory requirement is proportional to the number of unknowns. The algorithm has been used for the scattering solution of a 10 lambda -diameter 2-D scatterer with about 12000 unknowns, taking about 30 s on a CRAY-2 supercomputer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Single-frequency two dimensional Doppler imaging
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Using a unique form of target motion, two-dimensional images of the target are generated by a single-frequency CW (continuous wave) radar. This plus the limited range of aspect angles required for imaging places fewer constraints on the target than other known methods. As an example, a simulated three-target scene is imaged.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the singular value decomposition to aperture synthesis with boundary arrays
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown how arrays consisting of sensors arranged only on the boundary of a planar region can be used to synthesize the effect of a more densely populated array. Such boundary arrays can simultaneously achieve good resolution and low sidelobes, using relatively few sensor elements compared with 'filled' arrays. One essentially compensates for the missing elements from the interior of the boundary array by performing extra processing of the data. The authors focus on aperture synthesis techniques for passive imaging of spatially incoherent sources for some particular array geometries, namely the cross array and rectangular and triangular boundary arrays. Results are stated purely in terms of discrete arrays, and it is shown that the singular value decomposition provides a convenient solution to the aperture synthesis problem in this framework.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and development of wide band Dolph-Chebyshev antenna array in stripline form
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The design and development of a wideband (3.2-4.8-GHz and 2.0-12.0-GHz) Dolph-Chebyshev antenna array in stripline form are reported. Wideband equiphase power dividers were developed on the basis of a design approach proposed by L.I. Parad and R.I. Moynihan (1965) and S.B. Cohn (1968) for a 3.2-4.8-GHz unit. Experimental results for the individual power dividers and radiation plots of the composite unit are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Perturbation formulation for nearly-degenerate microstrip dipole eigenmodes
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: System eigenmodes of N-coupled, nearly degenerate microstrip dipoles are investigated through a singularity-expansion-based perturbation formulation. This method is based on integral-operator techniques employing rigorous dyadic Green's functions for the layered microstrip environment. Mutual coupling between microstrip antennas has been previously accounted for by full-wave formulations, and similar full-wave methods provide a comparison to this approximate formulation. System eigenmodes are found to form symmetry states about the isolated dipole eigenmode. The special case of N=2 coupled dipoles results in symmetric/antisymmetric coupling, which can be separated analytically.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive nulling of fully coherent interferences in a nonstationary signal environment
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An alternative approach for finding an optimal set of weights for antenna arrays which effectively nulls out fully coherent interferences is presented. Since the proposed technique does not require the signal matrix to be positive semidefinite the matrix can be formed at every observation time with the instantaneous values. The optimal weights are iteratively computed in a minimum number of steps at each snapshot. It is shown that the technique can be applied to the multipath problems occurring in mobile communication where the statistics of the signals may change at every observation time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of near-field operation on the collection efficiency of a freespace microwave power transmission system
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The collection efficiency between a circular aperture and a rectangular aperture is analyzed. A diffraction integral is used to calculate the near-field of the circular aperture. The calculated near-field is integrated over the rectangular aperture to determine the collected power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: In flight phased array alignment
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A method is proposed to perform an in-flight phase alignment on an airborne side-looking phased array when it is subjected to radome errors and scattering by the wings and engine nacelles. The capabilities of the Doppler radar processor are required to reduce the effects of clutter, and the factory alignment of the array is required to provide a useful transmit beam. The root-mean-square errors of the phase corrections are expected to be about 3.4 degrees .<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient technique for computing the response of a planar FSS as a function of the incident angle
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present an efficient method for computing the dominant mode (zeroth-order Floquet harmonic) scattering characteristics of a single-layer FSS (frequency selective surface) system for multiple angles of incidence. An interpolation procedure is considered where the most computationally intensive aspect of determining the currents and scattering parameters is carried out numerically rigorously for only a few incident angles, and computed via interpolation for the remainder. Some representative examples derived by using the cubic spline interpolation procedure are given, where the exact and estimated values of the transmission coefficient, S12, are compared, and the CPU times associated with these examples are quoted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gain measurements for a conformal active phased array
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A phased-array using T/R (transmit/receive) modules with gain on transmit and receive requires new antenna measurement techniques and data interpretation. On transmit the affected parameters include antenna aperture gain, antenna electronic gain, array effective radiated power, array power output, T/R module gain, and power output. On receive they include similar parameters, and array and T/R module noise figures. These measurement techniques have been developed during the testing of a linear array aperture with 64 microstrip patch radiators, flush mounted, conformal to a cylindrical surface. The measurement techniques as described in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Moving targets SAR processing
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The main results of SAR (synthetic aperture radar) processing are reviewed, and a method for imaging fixed and moving targets, called MTI (moving target indicator) SAR, at the same time is presented. The advantages and limitations of this method are explained. This is done in the framework of a side-looking airborne SAR, as opposed to spaceborne SAR.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Methods for minimizing the leakaged radiation of a non-selected array face
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Phase control methods for minimizing the leakage radiation of a nonselected array face are presented. The radiation patterns of an S-band triangular phased-array antenna with pin-diode phase shifter are calculated for the methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some new results of the Gram-Schmidt algorithm in DBF
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Some new results are obtained using the Gram-Schmidt algorithm (GSA) in digital beamforming (DBF). It is noted that the number of snapshot samples must be equal to the number of jammers: otherwise, the pattern nulls cannot be formed in the jammer directions. Both numbers can be determined adaptively. In addition, the amplitude and phase errors existing in each receiver and the GSA itself will affect the null position and depth of the difference pattern in the steering direction. These effects are eliminated in the algorithm described. It is also shown that the nulls in 2-D directions can be achieved by using the GSA in a planar array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: One-dimensional imaging of dielectric bodies of revolution based on Rayleigh approximation
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A one-dimensional profiling algorithm of lossy dielectric bodies of revolution which is based on the Rayleigh approximation is proposed. It is shown that the profile can be reconstructed adequately by performing the Fourier transformation of the backscattered field data in the frequency domain. The analysis and numerical examples presented are restricted to the axially symmetric target whose dielectric constant is known and nose-on incidence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An electromagnetic inverse problem in determination of certain 2D source distributions
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A method for determination of source distributions of planar structures is described. The inverse problem is formulated as an identification problem. The method consists of measurements of weak electromagnetic signals in the source region and inverse processing of the acquired data in order to retrieve information about spatial distributions. The source region Green's function is used in order to develop the inverse problem equations. Integrals are solved for the voltage of the sensing antenna in terms of unknown parameters of the source distribution. A numerical inverse problem equation is obtained through transformation of an analytical solution in terms of unknown parameters into a matrix equation. This transformation leads to a positive definite matrix of the system of simultaneous equations. An application of the inverse problem to the quality testing of multilayer printed circuit boards is included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-dimensional super-resolution with high gain beams
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The use of super-resolution to improve the performance of high gain monopulse antennas under main-beam interference and multipath conditions is evaluated. The geometrical theory underlying Schmidt's MUSIC algorithm is extended to multibeam signal processing antennas with directive beam patterns in azimuth and elevation. A new super-resolution algorithm is derived which is effective against both coherent and noncoherent signals. A conceptual design is described, and its detection and angle estimation performance for multiple signals incident in the mainbeam is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance investigations for typical mountings of a crossed-dipole and a quadrifilar helix
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Variations in performance are presented for a cross-dipole antenna and quadrifilar helix antenna installed in typical mountings. Installations that were investigated include a crossed-dipole over a finite ground plane, a quadrifilar helix mounted on a shaped ground plane, and a quadrifilar helix with shaped ground plane mounted on a representative side of a satellite. Measured radiation patterns are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reflection and transmission coefficients of a flat periodical array of magnetic metallic inclusions
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The author presents a theoretical study of the reflection and transmission coefficients of a flat periodic array of magnetic metallic inclusions. A spectral description of the diffracted fields coupled with a set of boundary conditions written on the top and the bottom of the inclusions is used. This makes it possible to write two equations where the magnetic and electric currents are, first, uncoupled and, second, directly associated respectively with the magnetic and electric incident fields. The solutions are obtained using the Galerkin method. The method shows that the response of a monolayer made of a periodic array of magnetic metallic inclusions (whatever their shapes) is weakly sensitive to the magnetic susceptibility of the inclusions. Nevertheless. the method is sensitive enough to allow one to recover the magnetic response of the composite from the reflection and transmission coefficients by solving the associated inverse problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Angle error simulation of radome effect for tracking phased-array radar
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The angle errors due to radome seam scattering are simulated for a tracking phased array at various mechanical and electronic scans. The dual antenna considered consists of an LFOV (limited-field-of-view) phased array and an FFOV (full-field-of-view) phased array. The 78 ft diameter metal space frame radome consists of high-strength metal seams joined together at hubs in such a fashion as to structurally approximate a shell capable of sustaining large loads. The computer simulations of the angle error due to the radome effect considered are valuable in trading off radome geometries and in supporting track analysis so as to arrive at a best system configuration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analysis of a coupled-ring rotary joint design
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A theoretical and experimental analysis of a coupled-ring rotary joint design is described. A rotary joint of this type is commonly used in multichannel radar designs. The main goal of the analysis is to develop a better understanding for transfer of energy through the joint's highly coupled rings. The author considers the geometry of a typical single channel and then describes a coupled transmission line model for the coupled-ring network. Using the model, he determines the type of ring network needed for low channel loss and small rotational variations of this loss. A series of measurements on some test models supports the predictions of the analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Educational software for microwave and millimeter wave planar structures
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The educational methodology used at the Department of Electrical Engineering of the University of Brasilia for the last two years is presented. The main objective of this methodology was to introduce modern concepts of analysis and synthesis of microwave and millimeter-wave planar structures, and their applications in the design of passive devices, to the students as well as to help them develop the 'feeling' which is required for designers. In this approach, analysis and synthesis tools for several different planar structures are developed from the theoretical fundamentals using modern computer-aided design techniques and thus forming a designer's kit. Afterwards, the software performance is evaluated through realization of various prototypes, in a closed-loop learning fashion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On computing the optimal weights for adaptive array processing
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Based on the Hermitian and Toeplitz properties of the signal correlation matrix, an approach to recursively compute the adaptive weights required for optimum processing of array signals is developed. The proposed approach finds the elements of the corresponding adaptive weight vector with size n from the elements of the adaptive weight vectors with size less than n. There are no matrix inversions required during the computation process. This results in a savings in the number of operations and storage locations. A simulation result demonstrating the proposed approach is given. Specifically, the application of the proposed recursive approach in adaptive array beamforming is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the time domain inverse scattering for the bistatic case
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A formula for calculating the far scattering field is proposed in the time domain. It is shown that this formula can be obtained directly from the expression of the far scattering field in the frequency domain by using the inverse Fourier transform. The relation between the bistatic and monostatic cases is found with this formula. Then the time-domain inverse scattering problem can be solved for the bistatic case. Therefore, a theory of inverse scattering has been developed. It can also be seen that the results of E.M. Kennaugh and R.L. Cosgriff (1958) and C.L. Bennett et al. (1973) are special cases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved accuracy of nonparaxial Gaussian beam (corrugated horn)
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The accuracy of a nonparaxial Gaussian beam is studied for the case of a corrugated horn. Modifications are given to the conventional Gaussian beam formulation derived using the paraxial approximation. With the modifications the field perpendicular to the beam axis can be calculated accurately with the Gaussian beam.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Propagation research on 20 GHz Earth-satellite paths with the DLR station
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: For the investigation of microwave propagation on 20 GHz satellite communication links, especially attenuation and depolarization by rain, a new measuring station was built at DLR Oberpfaffenhofen. The station consists of a 20 GHz beacon receiver, a polarimetric 20 GHz Dicke-radiometer, a coherent polarimetric C-band weather radar, and several meteorological instruments. This station is described, and results on differential sky temperature vs. absolute sky temperature, quasi-horizontal propagation, and copolar horizontal attenuation are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two dimensional angle and polarization estimation using the ESPRIT algorithm
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown how the ESPRIT algorithm may be used to estimate two-dimensional signal directions and polarizations with a polarization-sensitive array. The ESPRIT algorithm is a signal subspace method, which achieves computational efficiency by exploiting the spatial invariance properties of the crossed dipole array. With the ESPRIT algorithm, two-dimensional direction and polarization estimates are computed directly. The ESPRIT algorithm does not require a search over a multidimensional parameter space, as the MUSIC algorithm does.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modified subreflector design and diffraction analysis of Voyager's high gain antenna for Cassini spacecraft
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The Cassini mission requires that the reflector antenna be able to operate at four different frequencies. This means that in addition to the direct-fed S-band and Cassegrain-fed X-band operations, direct-fed Ku-band and Cassegrain-fed Ka-band operations are added on the Cassini antenna. A design scenario involving relatively simple and minor modifications to the existing Voyager dual-shaped symmetric antenna configuration is discussed. It is concluded that the subreflector displacement and the concomitant required surface reshaping, based on the phase-only geometrical-optics synthesis, is a good design alternative with an overall loss of less than 0.4 dB compared to that achievable with the original-shaped reflector, but still about 0.4 dB more than a nonshaped standard paraboloid/hyperboloid Cassegrain configuration, 5 dB more than a simple hyperboloid used with the shaped reflector, and several dB more than that achieved by simply moving the original shaped subreflector to a 1-in offset position.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A contoured beam shaped reflector antenna for broadcasting satellites
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A precisely shaped contoured beam antenna has been designed in the downlink frequency band (12 GHz) for future direct broadcasting satellites in Japan. The antenna consists of a single offset shaped reflector and a single feed horn. The single offset shaped reflector antenna was shown to radiate a contoured beam which covered the major part of the Japanese territory at over 40 dBi and other remote islands at over 28 dBi. The calculated radiation pattern was verified by measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The NSF/IEEE CAEME Center-what is next?
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Topics identified for future activities by CAEME (Center for Computer Applications in Electromagnetic Education) are briefly described. These include: use of evolving technology such as interactive video and multimedia presentation in its future software developments: development of software packages that complement the developed software in the first round of CAEME funding; and effective means for integrating CAEME software in undergraduate electromagnetics education.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new filter method for speckle reduction in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Conventional averaging of uncorrelated images of the same terrain to reduce speckle can be considered as filtering the image with a sinc-shaped filter. It is pointed out that this filter is poor in its spectral characteristics. A new filter with better characteristics, i.e., nearly flat passband and lower sidelobe-level is suggested. Examples are given to demonstrate the advantages of the new filter over the conventional one in terms of SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) improvement and spectral characteristics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Examining the appropriateness and effectiveness of computer-based interactive videodisc instructional models
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. During the past six years, the Institute for Interactive Technologies at Bloomsburg University of Pennsylvania has produced a number of computer-based interactive videodisc programs. Several of these applications are discussed with emphasis focused on the advantages, benefits and future challenges of learning technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spherical wave rotation in spherical near-field antenna measurements
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The rotation of spherical waves in spherical near-field antenna measurement is discussed. Considering the many difficult but interesting features of the rotation coefficients, an efficient rotation scheme is derived. The main feature of the proposed scheme is to ignore the calculation of the very small coefficients outside the ellipse. Therefore, not only will the underflow problem be eliminated but much computation time will be saved as well. An example is presented which shows the feasibility of the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Composite body-of-revolution and arbitrary surface analysis using the method of moments
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The need to predict the performance of a particular class of cavity-backed patch-fed antennas has motivated the development of combined body-of-revolution (BOR) and arbitrary surface analysis. The technique is general in the sense that it is useful for the radiation and scattering analysis of many objects which can be broken down into circularly symmetric portion and an arbitrary nonaxisymmetric portion. The use of special basis functions for the BOR part of the geometry results in substantial reductions in computation times as well as increased accuracy over using arbitrary surface models for the whole structure. Only the perfectly electrically conducting case is discussed. The cavity-backed antennas analyzed using the moment method are unique in that they are excited by large conducting patches in the plane of the aperture.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Input impedance and radiation pattern of spherical circular microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The spherical-circular microstrip antenna studied is a suitable element for the spherical arrays which can be used on top of vehicles for satellite communication. The input impedance of this patch is computed using the generalized transmission line model, which models the antenna as a transmission line loaded with wall admittance. The computed input impedance of the spherical-circular antenna is compared with that obtained from the planar circular disc when the sphere radius is large. The radiation patterns are computed using the method of moments and the aperture model. It is found that the radiation patterns computed from the two models are comparable whenever the dielectric thickness is small and the dielectric constant is small.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Magellan: a mission to map Venus
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Summary form only given. It was pointed out that not until Magellan has there been sufficient resolution to begin defining Venusian surface evolution processes. The Magellan Mission will cover at least 70% of the surface with resolution as good as 120 m. or an order of magnitude better than the best previous results. The mission provides an excellent example of economic and technical tradeoffs, involving radar system design, spacecraft design, mission design, and operational complexity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the FD-TD method to H-shaped rectangular optical waveguides
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The finite-difference-time-domain (FDTD) numerical technique is used to compute the dispersion characteristics of an H-shaped optical waveguide. The results are found to lie between the characteristics of a waveguide with a core-section surrounded by air and those of a waveguide with the same core-section that is surrounded by a cladding material. To verify that the FDTD method used here yields reliable results for mode dispersion characteristics of optical waveguides, the procedure outlined here is applied to examples of square waveguides that have been analyzed before. Numerical results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accuracy of local absorbing boundary conditions for use with the vector Helmholtz equation
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Frequency-domain procedures for 3-D electromagnetic scattering that are based on the vector Helmholtz differential equation must incorporate some form of radiation boundary condition to truncate the computational domain. Recently, a family of local absorbing boundary conditions has been developed for the 3-D vector case based on a general outward-propagating field. The authors present the error obtained using the 3-D vector absorbing boundary conditions as a function of boundary location and harmonic number. All the local boundary conditions degrade in accuracy as the harmonic index increases or as the radius of the boundary decreases. The error in the second-order condition is a significant improvement over that of the first-order condition and has been observed to be approximately the same for a given harmonic number as the second-order Bayliss-Turkel condition for the scalar problem. These results suggest that the second-order condition be used within numerical implementations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel ultra-wideband antenna
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present a novel ultra-wideband antenna that has been developed by combining two radiating structures, the slotline antenna and the bowtie horn antenna. It is shown that this antenna can maintain a stable pattern throughout a wide bandwidth, in this case 2 to 18 GHz, a flat plateau-like main beam, low sidelobes, low voltage standing wave ratio, (VSWR) and independent control of E- and H-plane beamwidths, Applications range from satellite communication applications to feeds for compact range reflectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering from perfectly conducting sinusoidal surface using the OSRC approach
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The on-surface radiation condition (OSRC) method is used to formulate the problem of scattering from a periodic, two-dimensional sinusoidal surface illuminated by a plane wave. In the OSRC method, a higher-order radiation condition is imposed directly on the surface of the scatterer. This will result in an analytical solution for the current distribution for the TM (transverse magnetic) case and an ordinary differential equation, for the TE (transverse electric) case. A comparison is made, for the TM case, between the present formulation, the exact solution, and the physical optics solution for a sinusoidal surface profile. The validity of the OSRC results is shown to depend on surface profile parameters and the angle of incidence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of higher-order splines and reciprocal-bases to the moment method solution of the electromagnetic scattering of three-dimensional flaw in anisotropic slab
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors outline the scattering problem of the anomalous conductivity within an anisotropic slab. They use the higher-order splines and their reciprocal bases in discretizing the E-field volume integral equation. The discretization is carried out by means of the moment method, in which the expansion functions are the higher-order splines and the testing functions are the corresponding reciprocal-basis functions. Hence, the method is not Galerkin, but the resulting matrix equation is quite regular. The significance of the new procedure is to introduce smooth volumetric currents within the anomaly region. The authors first present the theory of the higher-order splines and their associated reciprocal bases, and then show how it can be applied to discretize the E-field volume integral equation for a flaw in an anisotropic slab.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A broadband printed circuit antenna with strip grids
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A low-profile, L-band printed circuit antenna with large bandwidth (15% for VSWR <or=1.2, 23% for VSWR<or=1.5, and 31% for VSWR <or=2.0) and high gain (8.7 dB) is presented. The input impedance of the printed antenna is accurately calculated using the method of moments and the image theorem, and broadband complex impedance matching networks are optimized which are based on a lowpass prototype filter. Experimental studies of this element were performed, and large bandwidth was achieved, in agreement with the optimized result. This antenna is suitable for lightweight aircraft conformal structures, and can be used as a reflector feed.

articleTitle: The sectored cylinder: a model for scattering by bodies with cavities
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A mode matching method is used to add another class of test bodies for scattering by electrically large bodies. In the two-dimensional case these bodies consist of perfectly conducting cylinders which have one or more sectors replaced by penetrable regions. This class of shapes (called the sectored cylinder), bounded by circular arcs and radial straight sections, is very large and versatile and can describe bodies with cavities of various shapes, as well as strips, finite wedges, notched cylinders, etc. Selected results are presented which give confidence in the reliability of the present analysis and software and the suitability of the sectored cylinder to serve as an accurate test body.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Asymptotic high frequency computation of the RCS of a cone-sphere at an arbitrary angle of incidence
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown that the physical optics approximation, enhanced by correction terms, makes it possible to compute the RCS (radar cross section) of the cone-sphere for arbitrary angle of incidence. The validity of the method is established by comparing it with a numerically rigorous method of moments solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multifocal reflector antennas with multiple subreflectors
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors describe a focused multiple-beam reflector antenna consisting of a single offset-fed axisymmetric paraboloidal main reflector and multiple shaped subreflectors and feeds. Each pencil beam requires its own subreflector and feed unit, but duplicate feeds and subreflectors may share the main reflector to generate identical beams in different directions. The resulting beams may achieve high aperture efficiency. The principle of a dual-beam system which implements this approach is illustrated. The configuration of a Gregorian-type system that produces two identical unblocked beams 18 degrees apart is described to illustrate the approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Derivation of closed-form spatial Green's functions for printed circuit structures with substrates and superstrates
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A novel approach to deriving closed-form expressions for the spatial domain Green's function (vector and scalar potentials) associated with a horizontal electric dipole (HED) located over a thick substrate has recently been described. This technique is extended here to analyze a planar structure with both a substrate and a superstrate. The superstrate may form naturally on a printed antenna due to the weather conditions: it may also be deliberately introduced either as a protective cover or as a means to enhance the gain of a printed antenna by utilizing the substrate-superstrate resonances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel LU decomposition on a transputer array
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An important algorithm in linear algebra, i.e., LU decomposition, which initially seemed an unlikely candidate to benefit from parallel processing has been shown to be highly parallelizable. Results obtained with a moment method code on a transputer array show acceptable efficiencies for problems of interest in computational electromagnetics (CEM).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An omnidirectional microstrip antenna for mobile communications
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A circular patch antenna with TM/sub 0m/ mode for omnidirectional pattern has been analyzed and fabricated at 2.35 GHz using G-10 glass epoxy material. A VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio) of 1.42, a gain of 5 dB with respect to a lambda /2 dipole reference antenna, and an efficiency of 87% has been achieved. Close agreement between theoretical and experimental results has been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New boundary integral equation for waveguides with arbitrary cross-section embedded in a multilayered dielectric
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present a boundary integral equation to perform the full-wave analysis of coupled waveguides with arbitrary cross-section embedded in a general multilayered medium. The aim is to analyze the full range from dielectric waveguides via lossy conductors to perfectly conducting conductors. A domain integral equation has been shown to be well suited for waveguides with graded-index profiles. However, for lossy conductors, with homogeneous properties over their cross section, a boundary integral equation is preferable, due to the smaller number of unknowns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Combined GMT/SDT for EM scattering from an underground conducting cylinder
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A combined GMT (generalized multipole technique)/SDT (spectral domain technique) is proposed to solve the electromagnetic scattering of a plane wave from an underground conducting cylinder in parallel with the interface. The combined GMT/SDT is based on a simple model and rapid convergence. Some numerical results are provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interference by rain scatter-simulation of effects of real antennas on statistics
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Interference due to hydrometeor scatter between radio links at frequencies beyond 10 GHz is being extensively studied in view of the widespread use of these bands for terrestrial and space communication links. The author presents a study aimed at determining the statistical properties of interference, using real antenna patterns and a quasi-physical rain cell model. The procedures developed in this work can be used to perform a comparison with the results obtained using pencil beam antennas. The model was used to examine five simple cases of interfering links, both terrestrial and space.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental study of radar backscattering from simple targets
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A numerical method that was developed and applied to investigate the scattering properties of targets of prismatic shapes is used to study backscattering from cubes in the resonance region. The scattering properties of the same targets are determined experimentally at 10 GHz. The present method is extended to study the contribution of various modes, and the capability of the method as applied to corner incidence is studied. The geometry under consideration is a conducting cube and selected results for the backscattering are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rainfall rates statistics for several zones in Spain
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Rainfall-rate statistics for several zones in Spain are plotted and discussed. Particular attention is given to cumulative rainfall distributions for Barcelona, the middle Tajo Valley, and Western Andalusia, and to the monthly distribution of the average number of high rate events and average maximum rainfall rates for the middle Tajo Valley and Western Andalusia.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measured mutual coupling between two-layer electromagnetically coupled patch antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Measured mutual coupling results for two X-band rectangular EMCP (electromagnetically coupled patch) antennas are reported. Results for radiating edge (E-plane) coupling are shown for a single patch and for the cases when the EMCP is operating in the wideband region and the high gain region. Results for nonradiating edge (H-plane) coupling are shown. It is seen that high gain EMCP coupling via the radiating edges have the strongest coupling while the same antennas coupling via the nonradiating edges have the weakest coupling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parasite-free 3D finite element vector boundary-value solutions on C/sup 0/ elements
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Initial evidence is presented which supports the parasite-free nature of a specified Helmholtz-based weak form in three dimensions.
