The example of the penetration of electromagnetic energy through a shield with a thick gap in two dimensions is used to compare the methods. It is shown that the time per node is relatively constant for each method, but is considerably greater for the upwind scheme. It is also shown that the upwind algorithm resolves discontinuities in the medium better than the other techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dual-shaped dual-reflector antenna for a whispering-gallery-mode gyrotron
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A synthesis procedure based on the principles of geometrical optics has been applied to the design of a dual-shaped dual-reflector antenna used to transform the output of a gyrotron operating in a whispering-gallery mode to a Gaussian free-space beam. The new design is anticipated to improve the output-beam characteristics of previous antenna configurations in which the power distribution could be manipulated in only one dimension across the beam. This resulted in relatively poor free-space propagation characteristics and reduced coupling efficiency into guided wave systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RCS measurements of plate geometries with theoretical verification
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The rectangular plate is an important scattering geometry for examining multiple interactions between parallel edges, grazing-incidence scattering, corner-diffraction effects, and radar cross section reduction due to thin coatings. The authors present measurements, performed in an anechoic chamber, of several rectangular flat plate geometries, designed to emphasize the important scattering mechanisms that can be observed. High-frequency models, such as the method of equivalent currents for half-planes and for right-angled corners, and the uniform theory of diffraction, are used for verification and to illustrate weaknesses that still exist in high-frequency modeling techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An accurate 3-D solution of coplanar waveguides by the duality principle of dipoles and slots
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A highly convergent and accurate 3-D model for solving general coplanar waveguide (CPW) circuits is developed. This model uses the duality principle to convert the coplanar waveguide problem into two coupled strips problems for which a simple solution is easily obtained. To verify the accuracy of this model, the effective dielectric constant and characteristic impedance of the CPW are calculated and compared to available 2-D results. Very good agreement is obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite difference time domain algorithm in curvilinear coordinates for solving three-dimensional open-region scattering problems
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The finite-difference-time-domain (FDTD) algorithm is generalized to the curvilinear coordinate system and applied to the problem of electromagnetic scattering from a finite, perfectly conducting cone. The curvilinear FDTD algorithm employs a body-fitted grid for meshing up the computation domain and, consequently, is able to model the geometry of the scatterer with better accuracy than is possible with the staircasing approach conventionally employed in the FDTD algorithm. The problem of plane wave scattering from a conical target is used to illustrate the application of the curvilinear FDTD algorithm developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A UTD description of surface and space wave excitation at the edge of an impedance wedge
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The canonical problem of evaluating the field scattered at a finite distance from the edge of an impedance wedge which is illuminated by a line source is analyzed. Emphasis is placed on an analysis of surface wave excitation mechanisms. In particular, high-frequency expressions for the coupled surface wave-space wave contributions are presented. Also, suitable high-frequency diffracted field contributions are obtained to provide the continuity of the total field at the shadow boundaries of the surface waves.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A millimeter-wave compact range using an axially-symmetric paraboloid in a Gregorian configuration
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Some of the design aspects of a practical millimeter-wave compact range employing an axially symmetric main-reflector illuminated by a shaped subreflector are presented. Although in principle any reasonable surface shape can be used for the main reflector (all that is required is that it provides a reasonably small caustic region when illuminated by an incoming plane wave), a paraboloid of revolution is used here. This choice is partially motivated by the fact that axially symmetric paraboloids are readily available on the antenna market, and hence provide a cost-effective alternative. Once the subreflector surface has been determined, the geometrical optics field produced at an arbitrary aperture location by a given feed element can be calculated using ray optics. The final co- and cross-polarized levels of the aperture field of the compact range are shown. This system covers a frequency range from 18 to 170 GHz and boasts a measured quiet-zone region with dimensions exceeding half the main reflector diameter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Complete dyadic Green's function for three-dimensional nonradiating discontinuity analysis
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The magnetic potential vector approach is used to develop the complete dyadic Green's function for a three-dimensional discontinuity enclosed in a rectangular box loaded with a dielectric substrate. The electric potential vector is obtained by a simple transformation. These dyadic Green's functions are also obtained in special cases, and are in accordance with those published earlier.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparative study of several methods for reducing operation count in EM modeling
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A comparative study of several methods for reducing the operation count in EM modeling is presented. The computer time and storage are compared with the same example by using the moment method, the diakoptic method, the spatial decomposition method, and the matrix partitioning method. The features of each method are discussed. The scattering problem of a 2-D conducting strip with a TM (transverse magnetic) plane wave normally incident is chosen as a computational example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-layer patch backfire antenna
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown that an improvement in the electrical characteristics of the conventional microstrip BA (backfire antenna) can be realized by using a two-layer patch element instead of the usual patches. The new BA is well-suited for compact and medium gain applications, and is also attractive as a feed for paraboloidal antennas. Experimental results on radiation pattern, input voltage standing wave ratio, and gain are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Moment method solution for the RCS of a strip grating backed with reflector
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Periodic strip gratings have widely been used for the reduction of the radar cross sections (RCS) of metallic surfaces and also as frequency selective surfaces. A moment method solution is applied for the determination of the reflectivity from the periodic surfaces and hence the RCS is calculated. The results are verified experimentally. For the strip grating system, the RCS is found to be greatly reduced compared to the plane metallic surface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessing the error of transmission-line quasi-static analyses by means of a mixed finite element method
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A finite-element method (FEM) using a mixed formulation that provides lower bounds for the capacitance coefficients of microwave transmission-line structures is presented in conjunction with a standard formulation that gives upper bounds. The error of a FEM analysis may be assessed with this method. The mixed FEM can be easily applied to any geometry, representing an improved alternative to other formulations giving the same bounds but with certain limitations. Results and other features of the mixed FEM are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of rim loaded, axially-symmetric reflector antennas using integral equation techniques
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The application of integral equations to the analysis of thinly coated perfect electric conductors, in particular coated reflector antennas, is examined with emphasis upon the controllability of the far-field radiation patterns. A set of coupled-field integral equations, derived from enforcing boundary conditions and equivalence principle, represents the fields exterior and interior to the coating region and accounts for all of the scattering mechanisms associated with the problem. Results using integral equation techniques are presented which demonstrate the effectiveness that rim loading has in the control of the far-field patterns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An H/sup +/-plane Tee leaky-wave antenna
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A center-fed strip-loaded rectangular dielectric rod leaky-wave antenna is fabricated in such a way that the junction at the feed point appears as an H-plane Tee. Experimental studies on the H-plane Tee leaky-wave antenna with regularly spaced and AP (arithmetic progression)-spaced perturbations have been conducted. It is found that, in both cases, square radiation patterns with large beamwidth, low ripple amplitude, and sharp cut-off are obtained. Higher beamwidth and lower ripple amplitude are observed in the case of AP-spaced perturbations. These antennas may find application as feeds for deep cylindrical parabolic reflectors, where uniform aperture illumination with low spill-over is needed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High frequency scattering by a smooth coated convex cylinder simulated with higher order impedance boundary conditions
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present a rigorous uniform theory of diffraction (UTD) solution of the diffraction by a coated convex cylinder simulated with generalized impedance boundary conditions (GIBC). In addition, a uniform asymptotic solution is obtained which remains valid when the observation point is in the close vicinity of the cylinder. An important aspect of this work is the use of second-order GIBCs which are characterized by the inclusion of second-order field derivatives in their definition. Because of this, they are less local, leading to an improved simulation (with respect to the standard impedance boundary conditions) of the coating. The improved accuracy of the GIBC simulation is demonstrated, and it is shown how the presented UTD solution can be extended to treat multilayered coated cylinders.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Grating lobe characteristics of a hexagonal array of subarrays
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The characteristics of a hexagonal array formed by seven element hexagonal subarrays are described. It is pointed out that a hexagonal array formed with elements in a grid of equilateral triangles requires fewer elements than with a rectangular arrangement. Dividing a large hexagonal array into contiguous subarrays offers an economic and simpler way of building high-performance phased array antennas. The study of the performance of 3 hexagonal arrays indicates an overall improvement in the sidelobe structure and grating lobe level for one of the configurations considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gaussian beam and physical optics iteration technique for wideband beam waveguide feed design
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A novel approach is demonstrated which involves iterating Gaussian beam and beam waveguide (BWG) parameters to obtain a wideband BWG feed. The result is further improved by making a comparison with the physical-optics result and repeating the iteration. The basic goal was to design a BWG feed system with good performance from 2 to 32 GHz, utilizing mirror sizes of 20 lambda at the low frequency. The BWG antenna performance (e.g. gain, efficiency, noise temperature) at S, X, and Ka-bands is presented. It is noted that higher-gain horns are needed for higher frequencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High temperature antennas for the Hermes spaceplane
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: In order to survive reentry, the Hermes spaceplane is covered with a thermal protection system (TPS). In areas where antennas are located, two types are used: shingles in the hottest areas. and a flexible mattress in the less hot ones. The shingle TPS consists of C/SiC composite boxes filled with internal multiscreen insulator. The shingles are fixed to the aluminum spaceframe. The shingle antennas are integrated in the center of a shingle. Two concepts have been developed: a waveguide antenna and a patch cavity antenna. High-temperature tests have been performed on both concepts. In the tests the antennas were exposed to a thermal environment representative of an atmospheric reentry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A compact shaped single-reflector offset antenna with low cross-polarization
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A novel compact single-reflector offset antenna is presented. The antenna has been synthesized and analyzed by programs which result from modifications to corresponding programs for dual-reflector offset antennas. Computations have demonstrated that the novel antenna concept exhibits high antenna efficiency, low sidelobes, and low cross-polarization, similar to the pattern characteristics of dual-reflector offset antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Solution of inverse problems by the general maximum entropy method
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Many inverse problems are accompanied by a Fredholm integral equation of the first kind. The maximum entropy method (MEM) is extended and generalized to solve this equation with complex parameters and data. The iterative numerical algorithm of the general MEM is presented, and results of numerical simulation on electromagnetic inverse scattering are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An ISAR simulator for ships
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors describe techniques used to simulate ISAR (inverse synthetic aperture radar) images of ship models experiencing angular motions such as yaw, pitch, and roll. The simulation incorporates target modeling, radar scattering estimation, and image formation. It is pointed out that the ISAR and SAR simulators can produce very realistic images using the processing techniques described. The most critical procedure takes place during the construction of the ship model; the closer the model resembles the real ship, the more accurate the simulation will be. To some degree, the sea-state defined by the user will affect the amount of detail and ship structure information that can be extracted from the image.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of a high frequency Beverage antenna using a fiber-optic measurement technique
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: R.W.P. King (1983, 1990) has proposed a rigorous, generalized theory for the Beverage antenna above a dielectric half-space. The authors report extensive experimental and theoretical investigations that validate King's theory for a high-frequency Beverage antenna located above the earth. The antenna consists of a No.14 gauge copper wire, 180 ft in length, supported above the ground by wooden posts. One end of the antenna is connected to a signal source through a transformer/balun, and the other end is terminated in a suitable matched load. A novel fiber-optic measurement set-up has been used to measure the complex propagation constant (attenuation and phase velocity) of the current distribution along the antenna for various frequencies and antenna heights above ground. The amplitude and phase of the measured current distribution are shown to agree with those calculated from King's theory for two different antenna heights of 12 in and 64.5 in above the earth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Exact study of the implementation of a MESFET on a microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown how the association of the moment method and the theory of loaded scatterers appears to be an efficient mathematical tool for describing active microstrip antennas. The introduction of a MESFET on the feedline of an electromagnetically coupled microstrip dipole is analyzed as a case study. Theoretical results are in good agreement with experiment in regard to input impedance. It is concluded that the approach, which can be applied to any kind of two-port at any location in a radiating structure, provides a promising efficient tool for analyzing future microstrip phased arrays.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple scattering from two semi-circular bosses above the conducting plane
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The behavior of electromagnetic scattering from two unidentical semicircular bosses above a conducting half-space is investigated. Image theory is used to account for the specular reflection from the infinitely extended half space. Both incident and scattered fields are expanded in a Fourier series of azimuth angles with unknown coefficients. By enforcing the boundary conditions of the tangential E and H field continuity along two perfectly conducting circular cylinders, the expressions for the scattered fields are obtained. Numerical computations are performed to examine the bistatic and backscattering angular behavior of scattering coefficients, and their results are compared to single-scattering-approximated results. The relative importance of multiple scattering from two bumps is discussed in terms of bump-size, spacing, polarization, and operating frequency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Phase retrieval in near-field measurements by array synthesis
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The phase retrieval problem in near-field antenna measurements is formulated as an array synthesis problem. As a test case, a particular synthesis algorithm has been used to retrieve the phase of a linear array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compact representation of radiation patterns using vector spherical mode expansions
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A vector spherical mode expansion (VSME) method, extended from the scalar spherical mode expansion (SSME), is presented to study the radiation properties of an arbitrarily shaped antenna structure. The important difference between VSME and SSME is their expansion coefficients, which have essentially different properties. Numerical results show that VSME coefficients converge rapidly, while still yielding accurate data with a minimum number of modes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Plane wave diffraction by an anisotropic dielectric half-plane
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Plane wave scattering by a semi-infinite anisotropic dielectric layer, which can be considered as an example for electromagnetic energy absorbing materials, is investigated. By a formulation based on the Fourier integral transform technique, the scattering problem is reduced to two decoupled, scalar Weiner-Hopf equations. Diffracted, reflected, and transmitted field terms are evaluated using the Wiener-Hopf solution obtained with the standard method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering by a moving object: Computations and measurements
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors consider the relativistic scattering of a monochromatic electromagnetic wave by an electrically perfectly conducting object that moves with uniform velocity v in the x-direction of a stationary reference frame. A co-moving reference frame in which the object is at rest is also defined. The two reference frames are mutually related by the Lorentz transformation. A plane-wave representation of the incident field is used. These plane waves are transformed to the co-moving reference frame; they remain plane waves. The scattering problem in this co-moving reference frame is solved using the physical-optics approximation. The scattered field is written as a plane-wave representation. These plane waves are transformed back to the stationary reference plane; they remain plane waves. For low velocities of the object, numerical results pertaining to the electric field quantity are compared with experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of resistance in broadband, pulse-distortionless antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Radars that use baseband pulses, such as ground penetrating radars, require antennas that can radiate and receive temporally short, wide-bandwidth pulses. A variety of antennas have been proposed for this purpose. Usually these antennas incorporate resistive material to reduce reflections from discontinuities, such as the ends of a dipole antenna or at the open end of a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) horn antenna. The authors discuss two contributions resistance can make to the performance of these antennas: the aforementioned reduction of reflections along the structure and the preservation of the incident pulse shape on radiation. A simple canonical model is used: an open-ended parallel plate waveguide with a resistive (lossy) wall over a portion of its length. This structure is analyzed using finite-difference time-domain methodology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mutual impedance analysis of broadside coupled asymmetrical printed dipoles
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The mutual impedances of two-sided coupled asymmetrical printed dipoles are analyzed by using a spectral-domain method with a fast algorithm for the spectral-domain integration. The results for a special case of symmetrical structure with odd-mode feeding are compared with those for a microstrip dipole calculated by a moment method, and the open-end effect is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction method for oxygen attenuation on slant propagation path for 10-57 GHz
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Oxygen radiowave attenuation on slant paths is studied. A simple method for the prediction of oxygen attenuation on a slant path developed for the frequency range 10-50 GHz is discussed. The required input parameters for the method are temperature and pressure at the ground level. The method is valid up to 50 GHz, but it can be used with reduced accuracy up to 57 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time domain analysis of an array of tapered slot antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An efficient time-domain method based upon the combination of transmission line modeling or the finite-difference-time-domain method with an appropriate periodic boundary condition is developed. This technique is successfully applied to the time-domain characterization of a phased array of tapered slots.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A time-domain method for measuring the reflection coefficient of microwave absorbers at frequencies below 1 GHz
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A wideband time-domain reflectometer has been developed to measure the reflection coefficient of RF/microwave absorbers. The advantage of using a time-domain approach is that reflections from various parts of the test chamber can be separated from one another by the differences in their time of arrival at the receiving antenna. The resultant response waveform from a fire-retardant 940-mm rotated pyramid absorber after processing is complete is shown. In addition, measurement results are presented for a non-fire retardant and a fire retardant, 660-mm long pyramid.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reflector shaping by optimization of wavefront shapes
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The shaping of reflector antennas has generally been done by solving a system of partial differential equations (PDEs) which describe the ray tracking system. The technique has been very successful in many cases but has some difficulties with existence and uniqueness questions due to the PDE formulation. The author describes a technique which is based on direct optimization of the wavefronts in the system. The technique is very adaptable and has worked well in designing reflector systems for the Green Bank Telescope and dual reflector feeds for the spherical primaries at the Nancay and Arecibo Observatories.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Null synthesis for rigid and reconfigurable surface reflector antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Previous work is extended to include the synthesis of nulls in the antenna pattern, so that in addition to the specification of the high-gain coverage region of the pattern, one or more angles may be specified at which the antenna gain is to be minimized. An extension of this technique which allows low sidelobe levels to be enforced over specified areas of the pattern is also developed. A prototype mesh reflector antenna with a 28 lambda aperture and 52 control points on a 3 lambda grid has been constructed. A comparison of predicted and measured results is presented, showing generally very close agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient diffusive electromagnetic fields in layered anisotropic media
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The structural problem of the diffusion of transient electromagnetic fields in a stratified arbitrarily anisotropic conducting earth is investigated. In order to solve the equations governing the behavior of diffusive electromagnetic fields, an analytical method is developed based on the modified Cagniard method. Numerical results are presented. It is noted that one of the main advantages of using the modified Cagniard method is that it yields exact expressions in which arbitrary anisotropy is accounted for in the same way as isotropy, the only difference being that in the latter case simple and well known results can be obtained explicitly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New boundary integral equations for CAD of dielectric waveguide discontinuities
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The author presents boundary integral equations which are applicable to the basic theory of computer-aided design (CAD) software of many kinds of waveguide discontinuities. In order to understand the basic idea used in deriving the boundary integral equations, a rather simple problem, i.e., the transmission characteristics of a guided mode at a corner bend of the dielectric slab, is considered. Numerical examples of this simple problem establish the validity of the boundary integral equations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electronically controlled reconfigurable reflector antenna
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Results are presented showing antenna pattern reconfiguration using an electronically controlled surface. Spot-beam and shaped-beams have been generated and excellent agreement was found between predicted patterns and those measured at 10 GHz with a compact antenna range. The antenna comprises an 85-cm-diameter offset reflector fed from a 30 degrees corrugated horn. As an example of a typical shaped-beam, a template was chosen corresponding to a scaled version of an INTELSAT requirement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple beam antenna design for the Canadian EHF Satcom
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A multiple beam satellite system is being currently investigated by the Canadian Department of National Defence for possible applications in future military communications. The EHF Satcom will be operated in the 44/20 GHz links with high gain spot beams designed to provide Canadian coverage from a geosynchronous or a tundra orbit. The authors present the design of the multi-beam receive antenna system and its beam-forming network. Computed results of the antenna electrical performance are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multilayer patch antennas with multiple coaxial feed probes
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A mixed potential integral equation (MPIE) formulation is used to describe the currents on stacked patch antennas with multiple feed probes. The MPIE is solved using the method of moments. Simple rooftop and triangle basis functions are used on the patches and probes, respectively. Measured and computed impedance data are shown for a stacked patch antenna structure with a shorting pin attached to the lower antenna. It is noted that stacked patch antennas with multiple feed probes can provide wider bandwidth than single layer structures and can operate in two or more frequency bands. The model used to analyze these antennas, while not numerically simple, has fewer limitations than previous models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive Satcom antenna performance against blinking jammers
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The time-varying response of an adaptive multiple-beam antenna against various blinking jammers is investigated. The results provide useful design rules from which a robust adaptive process can be implemented. Several conclusions on how to implement robustness in an Howells-Applebaum processor (1966) are presented. First, changes in the jamming environment must be detected in real time, and the information must be fed immediately to the adaptive processor. Secondly, the processor must be capable of making changes in the algorithm convergence time to match the blinking rates of jammers. The processor must then be able to recall previous weight values and to reset weights as necessary.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Circular microstrip antenna array
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The radiated fields due to a circular array of patch antennas are investigated. The aperture method is used to determine the fields of the patch; for this initial study, the effects of mutual coupling are not included. The dependence of the radiated fields on the array geometry is examined for a frequency of 10 GHz and a substrate dielectric constant of 2.2. The practical applications of this array configuration are of interest for radar systems and air and space navigation systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of the Bologna cross radio telescope
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The Bologna Cross radio telescope operates at 408 MHz and consists of an east-west arm in the form of a large cylindrical reflector antenna 30 m * 564 m in extent and a second arm in the form of a large multiple interferometer arranged in the north-south direction. The feed characteristics and overall antenna performance of the east-west arm telescope have been calculated, and results not previously available have been provided. These results show that the original antenna was well-designed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering measurements for I-VII TC&R antennas on a spacecraft mock-up
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The optimal locations of the I-VII TC&R broadbeam antennas were determined based on scale mock-up test results. The broadbeam antennas at these locations will not only provide the best RF performance but also satisfy other spacecraft configuration constraints. It is shown that the I-VII H/Z reflectors create pattern blockage and a focused high X-pol on the telemetry antenna patterns. The computer predictions on these effects were verified by scale mock-up measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eigenvector analysis of isolated and coupled thin antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The boundary-integral method is used to solve for eigenvectors that are discrete representations of the characteristic modes of both single-layer and stacked thin microwave antennas. The performance of high-Q resonant devices is adequately represented near each natural frequency by a single characteristic mode. In the case of stacked structures, it is proposed that, instead of thinking in terms of the natural frequencies of the individual antennas (microstrip patches or cavity-backed slot antennas), performance (impedance and patterns) should be considered in terms of the multiple natural frequencies and corresponding characteristic modes of the coupled system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of series-fed, aperture-coupled microstrip arrays
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Series-fed resonant arrays of aperture-coupled antennas have been designed. Design curves have been generated that provide good accuracy when used in conjunction with standard array design methods. Arrays fabricated with these methods have demonstrated low sidelobe levels without special timing. An error analysis has demonstrated low sidelobe levels without special tuning. An error analysis has demonstrated that the primary limiting factor in low sidelobe performance was fabrication tolerances associated with the resonant length of the patch radiators. The errors in the resonant length of the patch antennas were estimated to be approximately +or-50 mu m and this produces about +or-14 degrees of phase error in the field radiated by the patches. For the array considered here, this limits the relative sidelobe level to approximately -25 dB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Vector space representation of array antenna pattern synthesis problems
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Considering the difficulties of the nonlinear optimization methods for the array and array fed reflector antenna power pattern synthesis problems, a novel approach has been developed to present the problem in a geographical way, which makes it possible to derive efficient algorithms and to visualize the optimization process. The vector space approach described provides a very powerful representation of the array pattern synthesis problems. It is not only general, since many parameters are represented under one model, but also helps to visualize the problem. The proposed approach provides a new support for optimization algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computation of big bodies with GMT: comparison between 2D and 3D cylinders (EM scattering)
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An attempt is made to compute the biggest possible 3-D body via MMP programs using PCs. The computation for a 3-D cylinder of 50 wavelength heights (radius 10 wavelengths) is performed. The near-field and the far-field qualities of the MMP codes are demonstrated. Previous results are evaluated by comparison with results for a 2-D cylinder.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lumped-element quadrature hybrids for wide-band antenna-feed networks
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A design tool based on existing techniques for broadbanding distributed couplers has been developed for application using lumped elements. The procedure enables the design of multisection and tandem couplers of specifiable bandwidth and ripple. Computer simulation demonstrates that technique produces a lumped element coupler performance which closely resembles that of the distributed prototype.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial nonuniform spacing of array elements
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The author describes a method in which all the elements are equally weighted and only the center elements are equally spaced. Elements towards the edge of the array are nonuniformly spaced to produce a low sidelobe array pattern. The spacing of the edge elements is computed using numerical optimization. Two examples demonstrate this concept.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental results for a thick skew-grid FSS with rectangular apertures at oblique incidence
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Theoretical and experimental results for the reflection characteristics of a thick plate containing rectangular holes on a skew grid at oblique angles of incidence are presented. By including a large number of waveguide modes in the solution, excellent agreement between theory and experiment has resulted. The use of a corrugated horn and lens allowed a high-quality test of the theory using a relatively small plate in the near field of the horn. The software is now being used to design thick frequency selective surfaces for high-power low-noise applications in the Deep Space Network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical and measured input admittance of a metal strip antenna contiguous with the edge of an electrically thick finite size dielectric substrate
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A technique for accurately calculating the input admittance of a metal strip antenna contiguous with the edge of an electrically thick dielectric substrate is presented. An efficient computational procedure to solve the coupled equations for the current on the strip and fields in the dielectric is developed. The results obtained have been compared with experimental results, and excellent agreement is obtained over a wide frequency range. Antenna elements similar to the one described may be useful in the construction of MMIC (monolithic-microwave-integrated-circuit)-based phased arrays at millimeter wavelengths.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CAEME software highlights
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Summary form only given. The Center for Computer Applications in Electromagnetic Education (CAEME) was established with the objective of providing leadership in the development of computer applications that will aid undergraduate education in electromagnetics. The author discusses the software that has become available with CAEME's aid and gives some impressions on its educational impact. A brief discussion of additional software needed to support undergraduate education in electromagnetics is also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 60 GHz beam waveguide antenna system
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A beam waveguide system has been designed by the use of the Gaussian beam formula and the optical mirror formula. Test results imply that the phase centers predicted by these formulas are quite accurate. It is shown that such a system can be fabricated without elaborate optical alignment procedure commonly used by optical engineers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mesh pillowing in deployable offset paraboloidal umbrella reflector antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An analytical formula capable of describing, with high accuracy, the offset paraboloidal umbrella reflector mesh shape is presented. This formula takes full account of the pillowing effect, and also applies to the front-end geometry, which is simply a degenerate case of an offset paraboloid. The basic steps used in deriving this formula parallel the ones used for the front-fed geometry. The validity of the analytical solution presented has been confirmed by comparison against a numerical solution obtained using the finite-difference technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of reconfigurable satellite reflector antenna for variable beam contouring
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors describe the electrical design of a reflector antenna where the reflector dish is reconformable such as to provide highly different contoured beams. A typical EUTELSAT coverage has been selected as the design driver for the present study. It is a requirement of the study that the surface material contain bending stiffness such that a smoother surface shape is obtained. A preliminary analysis indicates that a shaped reflector with an aperture diameter of 1.3 m will be sufficient to meet the required electrical performance. A parent paraboloid with the following dimensions has therefore been selected: aperture diameter 1.3 m, focal length 1.3 m, clearance between lower-edge and paraboloid axes 0.2 m.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radiation and scattering from infinite arrays of endfire slot antennas above a ground plane
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A Green's function-moment method analysis is used to investigate the radiation and scattering properties of infinite arrays of endfire slot antennas above a ground plane. The analysis utilizes the equivalence principle and a corresponding formulation which facilitates the extension of the analysis to antennas printed on protruding dielectric sheets and/or the addition of a radome. Numerical calculations are compared with waveguide simulator experiments for a linearly tapered slot antenna array as well as several less complex problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diffraction by a symmetric material junction. I. General solution
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Generalized impedance boundary conditions (GIBCs) and generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) have been explored as a means of modeling thicker material layers. Unfortunately, the resulting diffraction solutions obtained with GIBCs and GSTCs are often nonunique, typically displaying unknown constants which cannot be determined after the application of the standard edge condition. The authors address the general solution and the subsequent determination of the unknown constants for three specific junction geometries. Particular emphasis is placed on diffraction by grounded metal-dielectric junctions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering of EM waves by a wire grid of linear and non-linear wire segments
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An enhanced wire grid model is considered for the study of scattering of electromagnetic waves by an electrically large object. In addition to the straight wire, a canonical element, namely, an arc with a finite radius of curvature, is introduced. An accurate, yet computationally efficient, technique can thus be developed for determining the current induced on the surface of this canonical element. With the present formulation, simplicity and elegance can be retained. As a demonstration, grid models representing a cylinder, a cone, and a sphere are depicted. The development of a technique for determining the current induced on the surface of a given arc is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A proposal on integralization design, diagnosis and regulation of ultra low side lobe array of dipoles
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A proposal on integralization design, diagnosis, and regulation of an ultralow sidelobe array of dipoles is presented. Through the decoupling matching network, the integralization design is simplified. This network also provides the means to regulate the current distribution after the near-field diagnosis is performed. A ten-element array with 60-dB Chebyshev distribution was designed to demonstrate the proposal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis for MM/GTD of circularly polarized dual beam antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Consideration is given to a monopole antenna with a planar finite reflector and especially with a disk reflector made of a perfect conductor. A hybrid analysis method consisting of the moment method and geometrical theory of diffraction (MM/GTD) is used to calculate the effects of antenna reflectors, especially those of the edge of a circular finite reflector, on the input impedance and directivity of the antenna system, and experiments on several examples of such a system are performed. Assuming the direction and number of elements of the monopole antenna to be arbitrary values, the effects of diffractions due to the reflector's edges are considered on the basis of the GTD.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recursive T-matrix algorithms for 1-D and 2-D clusterings of strips
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Two recursive T-matrix algorithms were introduced for EM scattering by W.C. Chew (1989), W.C. Chew and Y.M. Wang (1990). In the present work, the authors discuss the application of these algorithms to conducting strip geometries, and analyze the complexities of the algorithms. The two algorithms are shown to have complexities of O(N/sup 2/P) and O(NP/sup 2/), where N is the number of unknowns in the problem, and P is the number of terms that satisfies a convergence criterion in the addition theorems for the cylindrical wave functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Input impedance and cross polarization studies of EMCP antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Experimental results on the input impedance characteristics of the two-layer electromagnetically coupled patch antenna as a function of feed position and layer spacing are presented. The input resistance is shown to increase as the feed is moved away from the center. For a given feed location, the input resistance decreases with increasing Delta (air gap spacing). Results on the cross polarization level of the antenna are also reported. The cross polarization level was found to change somewhat with Delta . However, for the range of values studied, it remained at least 30 dB below the copolarization level at boresight, provided the feed location from the center is chosen so that the return loss is >or=10 dB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The MMP applied to the scattering problem of the periodical array
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The MMP is applied to the 2-D scattering problem of the 1-D periodical array, which is constructed of a cylinder element with the cross-section composed of piecewise linear, homogeneous, isotopic materials. The basic principle and the problem-solving steps are introduced. As examples, the resultant fields of the array are constructed of the cylinder element with the cross-section of dielectric-coated conducting disc, separated dielectric elliptical and conducting circulating discs, and partly conducting and partly dielectric geometrically irregular disc, as solved by the proposed method, are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Suppression of reflection from slots in a linearly-polarized radial line slot antenna
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present a new slot design for a single-layer linearly polarized radial line slot antenna which suppresses the reflection from slots. The design procedure of the array is presented. A slot set is optimized to minimize the reflection. Then, sets are arrayed all over the aperture to realize uniform aperture distribution. The design is confirmed by measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Propagation in surface ducts over irregular terrain
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The implicit finite difference/Green's function method has been used to analyze the effect of ground roughness and a terrain obstacle on propagation within a surface duct. The effect of mode conversion and roughness amplitude was clearly exhibited. The method can be used to analyze propagation in elevated duct environments in hilly terrain where mountain peaks penetrate the duct. It can also be used in standard and duct environments that vary horizontally. It is noted that the efficiency and stability of the method make it an ideal candidate for extension to three-dimensional geometries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 3D vector variational hybrid finite-element/boundary element formulation for the scattering analysis of arbitrary infinite doubly periodic arrays
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors summarize a very general vector variation E-field formulation for the problem of plane wave scattering from infinite doubly periodic arrays of volume cells. The cells may contain 3D arbitrary and possibly composite scatterers. The stationary functional was derived using the general variational electromagnetics methodologies of S.K. Jeng (1983). The exact radiation boundary condition is absorbed into the variational functional via surface patch boundary elements. The volume is discretized using tetrahedral edge-based vector finite elements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The method of relative phase applied to wire-type scattering structures
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The method of moments in conjunction with the method of relative phase is used to determine the radar cross section (RCS) response from a collection of planar wire-type elements which may conform to a cylindrical surface. The method of moments is used to define the scattering matrices of each wire-type element which completely describes the object in 4 pi -space within a given bandwidth. The individual element responses are then combined using the relative phase differences, with the assumption that the phase-center is at the center of the wire object. Correlation is good between relative phase approximation predictions, moment-method predictions, and RCS measurements for element-to-element spacings greater than one wavelength. Two cases were investigated between 6-18 GHz for vertical polarization: (1) a loosely spaced arrangement of 4 star elements of the same size; and (2) a closely spaced arrangement of 17 star elements of different sizes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Beamwaveguide optics designs for implementing an electronic tracking feed on reflector antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present beamwaveguide (BWG) optics designs for implementing an electronic tracking feed on reflector antennas. The emphasis is on developing a compact BWG optics design for a 34-m reflector antenna in the NASA JPL Deep Space Network subject to the space constraint of its front equipment room. The compact design also has a cost advantage from using a much smaller mirror of high-precision surface. It is most suitable where a tracking function is needed at high frequencies. A diffraction analysis verification of the compact design is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sidelobe minimization in array fed dual reflector antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Results from recent studies aimed at optimizing array-fed dual-reflector antenna concepts with respect to peak sidelobe level are presented. The dual reflector antennas studied were confocal parabolic Cassegrains. Center-fed and offset-fed designs were considered, with emphasis on center fed. A small amount of beam steer, up to about 3/4 beamwidth from broadside, was considered as well. The essential geometrical features of the concepts are shown. The relative sizing and positioning of the feed and reflector elements were varied in attempting to minimize the peak sidelobe. The analyses were based upon physical optics. The large reflector apertures were several hundred wavelengths in diameter. Parameters that were studied included the feed amplitude distribution, feed array location, magnification, focal length to diameter ratio, and reflector oversizing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new algorithm of scattering from a finite periodic surface-conjugate gradient-circular convolution (CG-CC) method
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A conjugate gradient-circular convolution (CG-CC) method of analyzing scattering from a finite surface with multiple periodicity is presented. This method may improve the accuracy and convergence of the solution by eliminating the aliasing effect introduced by the truncating procedure or periodical extension of the structure. Numerical results of the induced current distributions on 1-D and 2-D dipole arrays are presented and compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of a microstrip patch antenna including a coplanar feed
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A rectangular microstrip patch antenna with coplanar feed is analyzed by the spectral domain method. The radiation patterns calculated from the current distribution are compared with measurement data and presented. Both theory and measurement predict the same input impedance match at 7.6 GHz and 18.475 GHz. The current distribution on the feed line is shown to have a strong influence on the cross-polarized field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Method of moments formulation for an arbitrary material configuration
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A method-of-moments surface formulation for an arbitrary material configuration is presented. The material effects are included via an exact formulation rather than by using approximate boundary conditions such as the surface impedance model. Furthermore, complicated material composition such as a multilayer coating can be accommodated. The equivalence principle is applied to the multiple conductor/dielectric body configuration in order to obtain an equivalent scattering problem for each homogeneous medium existing in the model. Superposition of all equivalent problems results in the solution of the original problem. To solve for the equivalent currents on the bodies involved in the problem, the method of moments is applied to the PMCHW (Poggio, Miller, Chang, Harrington, and Wu) formulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Millimeter wave dielectric measurements at elevated temperatures
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Interest in the constitutive parameters of materials at elevated temperatures continues to increase as new materials are developed for high-temperature applications. A simple, relatively nondestructive method for testing materials at millimeter wave frequencies is presented here. Measurements have been performed between 30 and 100 GHz at temperatures up to 1500 degrees C in a commercially available furnace. Measurements to date have been performed on dielectric materials with dielectric constants ranging from 1.2 to 10. The measured dielectric constant and loss tangent of a low-loss foam material are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A scheme to obtain propagation characteristics of multilayer structures using spectral methods
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An application of the conjugate gradient method in combination with the fast Fourier transform (CG-FFT) for the analysis of multilayer structures is presented. The first step in the process is solving the electric field integral equation (EFIE), which is done using a sampling procedure with rooftop functions to represent the induced current and pulses to average the fields. The second step is the computation of the field components at different levels of the structure. Finally, these data can be used to compute the desired parameters for microstrip circuit design purposes. Results obtained with the proposed scheme are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Circular polarization characteristics of parasitic microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The circular polarization (CP) characteristics of an electromagnetically coupled patch (EMCP) antenna of both coplanar and stacked geometries have been studied experimentally. Compared to the single CP patch antenna, the EMCP antennas were found to have better axial ratio bandwidth and directivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A seven patch hexagonal CP subarray with CPW/stripline feed network
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A seven-element microstrip subarray of hexagonal geometry has been designed and tested at S-band frequencies. The microstrip patch antenna is excited at a single-feed position using a direct-type connection to generate a circularly polarized (CP) wave. The RF power is coupled to these feed positions by a novel coplanar waveguide/stripline feeding network. The subarray architecture and the feed network are described in detail. The measured results include the feed network characterization and the radiation patterns of the subarray.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aperture-coupled patch antenna-theoretical and experimental investigations
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The spectral domain analysis of a slot-fed rectangular patch antenna is presented. The equivalent circuit of the structure is obtained and elements in the equivalent circuit are determined using the integral transformation technique. The slot is considered to be inclined to both feed line and the patch. Effects of various slot parameters, such as slot length and angle of inclination, on the resonance and on the input impedance are studied. Numerical results for the input impedance are found to agree with the measured data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dual reflector polarization transformers
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A few different kinds of first-order partial differential equation (PDE) are presented to shape the subreflector surface in a dual-reflector antenna, transforming the given polarization distribution of the incident toroidal wave to that given over the plane wave. The main reflector is calculated as soon as the subreflector is known. Varying the tore radius from zero to infinity, the subreflector surface PDE can be obtained for many important cases, namely for spherical, cylindrical, or plane incident waves. The beginning value for the PDE-arbitrary subreflector curve is still free and may be chosen to minimize any prescribed object function. The results are derived under the geometrical-optics approximation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modal expansion analysis of discrete source scattering by a spherically stratified lens
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An eigenfunction expansion into the standard vector spherical wave functions is used to compute the scattering of electromagnetic radiation by a spherically stratified object. The incident field is that of an infinitesimal current element (a point source) and not a plane wave. Its expansion coefficients are obtained by matching the far field. The coefficients for the scattered fields are then determined from the boundary conditions at each interface, at the origin and at infinity. This analysis is employed to determine the radiation properties of a dielectric lens at microwave frequencies. The work is extended to include the scattering of other sources such as horns and microstrip patches which are then used in conjunction with the lens to form a multiple-beam antenna.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical analysis for the scattering by a waveguide cavity with complex configuration
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown that coupling wave theory combined with the finite-element method can be used to treat scattering by a waveguide cavity of complex configuration. This technique is efficient and accurate; it can manage to calculate the scattering from a curved and variable cross-section tube. Experimental and numerical results have verified this.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Charts for a quick design of microstrip line fed patch antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present charts for a quick design of two microstrip patch antennas both fed by a microstrip line, one by EM coupling and the other through an inserted low-impedance coplanar section. These design charts have been used in several practical applications and have therefore been extensively subjected to experiments and indisputable success. Such charts can be introduced into the library of any microwave CAD (computer-aided design) software as user look-up table models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Maximum super angle optimization method for array antenna pattern synthesis
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Different optimization criteria related to antenna pattern synthesis are discussed. Based on the maximum criteria and vector space representation, a simple and efficient optimization method is presented for array and array fed reflector power pattern synthesis. A sector pattern synthesized by a 20-element linear array and a narrow, sector beam with very strict sidelobe specifications are considered as examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of frequency scanning elliptical array
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is considered that the radiation field of an end-fed elliptical array whose main beam points toward the array normal and whose elements are equally-spaced in the ellipse is the output of a time-invariant system. On the basis of the linear system, the transfer function of this system is obtained and the formula is presented. The time required for the establishment of a steady pattern is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of angles of arrivals of multiple wideband sources
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors have developed a data transformation matrix for the estimation of directions of arrival for multiple wideband sources when prior information about the source locations is not available. The proposed focusing matrix minimizes the average of the squared norm of focusing error over the angles of interest without prior knowledge of source locations. This data transformation matrix does not require the preestimates which existing focusing matrices need. Using this data transformation matrix, one can remove the computational burden of preestimation. Simulation examples are used to evaluate the performance of the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonsidelobe unidirectional backfire arrays with small array width
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A unidirectional backfire array is realized when the summation of each amplitude coefficient is zero and its phase difference corresponds to the distance from the first element. This array has a nonsidelobe pattern when the array width is less than or equal to the quarter-wave length. The relation between the backfire array pattern configuration and the curvature-radius at the mainlobe direction is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new time delay concept using integrated optics techniques
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An integrated optic time-delay unit is described which relies on a folded path optical waveguide to achieve time delays ranging from a few picoseconds to several nanoseconds. The folded path configuration utilizes thick phase gratings as reflective elements. These elements provide large angle deflection, high diffraction or reflectivity, and wavelength multiplexing capabilities, and form the basis for an electronically addressable switch. By cascading gratings or alternatively utilizing long gratings, the transmitted optical signal is expected to be reduced to -40 dB to -60 dB or better, thus offering excellent isolation. The folded path configuration is the key to a small compact package. Using low loss waveguides, it is projected that time delays up to 10 ns can be achieved in a package size of 25 mm by 75 mm. The delay line concept, with the exception of active switching, has been demonstrated using ion exchange waveguides and surface relief gratings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of a concurrent adaptive least-squares sidelobe cancellation system with excess degrees of freedom
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present an analysis of the performance of a concurrent blocked sidelobe canceler when there are more auxiliary array elements, or degrees of freedom, than spatially coherent interferers. The existence of an excess degrees-of-freedom problem for the concurrent processor is reconsidered. The main result is the analytic determination of tight bounds for the mean square error for the concurrent blocked sidelobe canceller in the excess-degrees-of-freedom region. The performance of a sidelobe canceller applied to a 1000 element planar array having a circular aperture with a radius of 100 wavelengths is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave integrated diagonal horn antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A high-efficiency integrated horn antenna has been designed for millimeter-wave applications. The design consists of a dipole antenna suspended on a dielectric membrane along the diagonal of a pyramidal cavity etched in silicon. The theoretical far-field pattern and input impedance of the dipole-fed horn antenna are calculated using full-wave analysis. The impedance and radiation patterns of a dipole-fed diagonal horn antenna were measured at microwave frequencies. It is found that a dipole feed position of 0.4 lambda and horn apertures between 1.0 lambda and 1.4 lambda yield nearly equal E- and H-plane patterns. The associated directivity for a 1.35 lambda horn aperture is 9.8 dB+or-0.2 dB. The resonant feed dipole input impedance is 55 Omega and suitable for Schottky diode and SIS detectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Co/cross polarized antenna feed design
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The design and development of a novel, low-cost, co/cross-polarized feed is reported. Its application is part of a reflector antenna system used in VSAT (very small aperture terminal) networks operating over the C-band frequency range (transmit 5.925-6.425 GHz and receive 3.7-4.2 GHz). The challenging design parameter of this feed was to provide both copolarization and cross-polarization configurations in a single component.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determining excitation coefficients of dual-frequency shaped beam linear array antennas for mobile base station
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The sidelobe level increase of a dual-frequency linear array antenna is numerically analyzed from the viewpoint of base station antenna design. The analysis results suggest the following: frequency separation and element spacing can be determined for target tilt angle to avoid sidelobe increase caused by the influence of grating lobes. The sidelobe increase created by phase distribution error is shown throughout the frequency band. It is shown that the increase is more critical at the lower frequencies. A method of determining optimum excitation coefficients is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering and radiation from microstrip patch antennas and arrays residing in a cavity
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A hybrid numerical technique for characterizing the scattering and radiation properties of microstrip patch antennas and arrays residing in a cavity which is recessed in a ground plane is presented. The technique combines the finite-element and boundary integral methods to formulate a system for the solution of the fields at the aperture and those inside the cavity via the bioconjugate gradient method and fast Fourier transform. By virtue of the finite-element method, the proposed technique is applicable to patch antennas and arrays residing on or embedded in a layered dielectric substrate and is also capable of treating various feed structures and impedance loads. Several numerical results are presented, demonstrating the efficiency and capability of the technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Iterative methods for an inverse scattering problem of a three-dimensional flaw in anisotropic slab
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A rigorous and efficient scheme based on coupled integral equations is proposed to circumvent the limitation of the Born and Rytov approximations. In this scheme, one forward and one inverse problem will be solved at each iteration. During the forward-phase, one updates the unknown electric field within the object, while during the inverse-phase the estimate of the conductivity of the object will be updated. The inversion algorithm for this scheme is based on conjugate gradients and the fast Fourier transform. This method is suitable for least-squares, overdetermined problems with many unknowns (i.e. several thousand).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new procedure for interfacing transmission line matrix (TLM) method with frequency-domain solutions
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present a procedure that interfaces the transmission-line matrix method with frequency-domain solutions of electromagnetic fields. Hence, the corresponding boundary Johns matrix can be determined with minimum computational effort. Good results were obtained and a substantial CPU time reduction, compared with other approaches, was observed.
