Applications of the proposed approach to wideband absorbing boundaries in waveguides and to highly conductive shields are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Flat energy density antenna
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present a feed circuit for the flat energy density antenna for mobile telephone, and measurement results on its input characteristics and radiation pattern at 1.5 GHz. The correlation coefficient between ring patch and notch antenna of less than 0.1 is small enough for diversity branches. To verify the diversity effect of this antenna, the authors measured urban propagation characteristics at 900 MHz and compared them with results for a space diversity antenna. It is confirmed that the flat energy density antenna is appropriate for the diversity antenna of a mobile telephone.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency reactive doublers design with maximum efficiency
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A general, simple, and fast method for designing reactive doublers which takes into account the technological limitations of the structures chosen for its realization has been developed. The method is composed of the following steps: characterization of the nonlinear component, design of the doubler using the Burckhardt (1965) equations and nonlinear simulation. It is concluded that computer-aided design techniques make it possible to optimize simple nonlinear structures, like doublers, by a successive approximation method. The quality of the simulation is such that it allows the choice of the most adequate topology for adaptation circuits. The close agreement between the theoretical and experimental results shows the validity of the method chosen.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RCS calculation for penetrable bodies of revolution using FDTD
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An attempt was made to determine if the FDTD (finite-difference-time-domain) could be successfully applied using cubical cells to compute RCSs (radar cross sections) for smooth bodies of revolution composed of lossy dielectric materials. The bodies considered were a sphere, an oblate spheroid, and a spherecone-oblate spheroid. These shapes were modeled in three dimensions using cubical cells, and RCS calculations were made by Fourier transform of the far-zone time-domain scattered fields computed by FDTD. The results indicate that for penetrable targets the far-zone RCS calculated using cubical FDTD cells can in many cases be sufficient for estimation of the scattering amplitudes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A visual electromagnetics laboratory for engineering education based on TLM
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A new educational tool in the form of an electromagnetic wave simulator is described. It is based on the transmission-line matrix (TLM) method of numerical analysis (a method using Huygens's principle in discretized form), employs a sophisticated graphics user interface, and runs on MS DOS computers, as well as RISC (reduced instruction set computer) workstations. Since most students now have access to such machines, it becomes feasible to employ this field simulator as a visual electromagnetics laboratory, complementing the traditional teaching of microwave courses. The main features of the TLM wave simulator are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient aperture formulation for large scattering problems
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A method for reducing the number of unknowns for large scattering problems while maintaining a predetermined computation time, using a smaller matrix formulation, is discussed. The suggested approach is based on an aperture. rather than surface formulation, with the electric aperture field as the primary unknown. One eliminates from the computation the components of the unknown for which the solution is known, leaving a minimal portion of the field to be computed, the aperture part of the field that is related to the fringe current component. It is found that the equivalent incident current serves as a major tool for simplifying the equations. The resulting integral equation uses the equivalent incident current over the truncated aperture as the driving function, and the fringe current portion of the electric field over this region is the only unknown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of an insulated antenna in an arbitrary homogeneous medium
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An insulator dipole with axisymmetric geometry in an arbitrary medium is studied. The radiation properties of electromagnetic fields of such an antenna are investigated. It is demonstrated that the surface of integration should be closed because the currents on the caps of the insulator make a significant contribution to the fields and input impedance of the insulator dipole. It is observed that the insulated antenna has a more uniform near field along the antenna than the bare antenna. Also, it is seen that the coating material changes the effective length, near field, and input impedance of insulated antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multimode Gaussian beam point-matching program for analysis of beam guides
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A program for analysis of asymmetry and cross-polarization losses in reflector beam guides, based on Hermite-Gaussian beam expansions, is described. When executed on a supercomputer, the program is fast enough to be used for interactive design or optimization. The coefficients of the reflected modes are found from a least-squared error fit to the boundary conditions at a number of sample points. The results are compared with analytical solutions which are available in the case of a zeroth-order beam reflecting from an ellipsoidal mirror, and data are presented for reflectors with random surface deviations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient analysis of large reflector antennas under pulse-type excitation
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Unavoidable transient phenomena may affect the performance of reflector antennas used in pulsed radar systems. Time-domain physical optics is used to analyze such transient phenomena as transient-induced signal distortion. Analyses are made of the transient-state of a reflector antenna with pulse-type excitations and of the transient-time of a large paraboloidal reflector. Results are presented in a form suitable for radar system design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Contoured-beam synthesis by optimisation of BFN component values
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: A contoured-beam synthesis procedure for a multiple-feed antenna is presented. In this procedure the optimization algorithm operates on the beam-forming network (BFN) component values in order to maximize the level in the desired farfield region. A database containing S-parameter information about Ku- and Ka-band components is included in the synthesis procedure. Hence, the optimization is carried out taking the frequency behaviour and the imperfections of the BFN components into account.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of compact range using a diagonal flat plate
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The authors present a method which uses a diagonal flat plate to develop a stray signal criterion based on a tolerable RCS (radar cross section) measurement error. The scattered cross section of a 1.25 ft by 1.25 ft diagonal flat plate has been measured in a compact range with a blended rolled-edge reflector and with a knife-edge reflector. The measured RCS pattern of the plate at 6 GHz is shown, with the ideal plate RCS pattern plotted for comparison. The stray signal from one of the junctions between the rolled edge and the parabolic section is about 6.2 degrees from the axis of the plate. As a result, there should be an error in the plate RCS pattern at approximately=3.1 degrees . It is found that this error is about 0.88 dB for the blended rolled-edge reflector. The knife edge of the modified reflector is located about 12 degrees from the plate axis and, as a result, there is a significant error (5.17 dB) in the plate RCS pattern at theta =6 degrees .<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved conjugate gradient FFT method for 2-D TE scattering problems
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is pointed out that the problem of two-dimensional scattering of a transverse electric (TE) polarized wave by a dielectric object can be formulated in terms of a hypersingular integral equation, in which a grad-div operator acts on a vector potential. The vector potential is a spatial convolution of the free-space Green's function and the contrast source over the domain of interest. A weak form of the integral equation for the unknown electric flux density is obtained by testing it with roof-top functions. As the next step, the vector potential is expanded in a sequence of the roof-top functions and the grad-div operator is integrated analytically over the dielectric object domain only. Numerical results are presented for a lossy dielectric coaxially layered cylinder. The method considered shows excellent numerical performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hypermedia approach towards teaching physics
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Summary form only given. Four aspects of introductory physics courses at Harvard in which computers and hypermedia play a role are discussed. These are: a 'course-interface' shell that allows students to interactively enroll, organize, and participate in a course: computer-based animations for classroom use: Essence of Physics, a HyperCard-based interactive study guide used by the students: and computer-based 'physics intuition' tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spherical wave expansions for reflector antennas with truncated field data
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Spherical wave expansions (SWEs) for focus-fed symmetric paraboloids and hyperboloids using truncated field data have been investigated. The input field data for obtaining the SWE coefficients of a symmetric reflector have been determined in terms of numerical single integrals using the formulation given by A.W. Rudge et al. (1986). Patterns obtained for a hyperboloidal reflector are shown. These patterns indicate that the on-axis accuracy of the patterns produced from truncated field data is determined by the pattern intensity at the truncation angle. Truncation at a point of relatively high field intensity results in an appreciable ripple level for the on-axis field amplitude as a function of distance from the reflector.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the modeling of the impedance boundary condition in the time domain
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: It is shown how the impedance boundary condition can be extended to the time domain. Details of its implementation are shown for the time-domain-finite-volume method previously developed by the authors (1991). Only the first-order impedance boundary condition is considered. The radar cross sections for a dielectric-coated perfectly conducting cylinder computed for three different values of surface impedance by this method are shown. They compare very well with the series solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical transmission and switching technologies for broadband telecommunication networks
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Summary form only given. Advances in optical devices for applications in broadband telecommunication networks were discussed. Starting with basic optical fibers, semiconductor lasers, and photodetectors, the author covered optical devices for coherent optical communications, optical amplifiers, and optical switching as well as optical passive devices. In addition, advances in optical transmission and switching systems made possible by the evolving optical technologies were discussed as well as their impact on the viability of the broadband telecommunication network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FDTD method for electromagnetic coupling through composite material with contact resistance
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: An attempt has been made to improve the FDTD (finite-difference time-domain) formalism for electromagnetic coupling through composite material by taking into account the imperfect contact between the loading material and the rim of the aperture. The low frequency domain is still assumed. The results of the FDTD code ALICE are first compared with analytical results. A code validation is then obtained with experimental data. Experimental transient electromagnetic fields were obtained on the French military Transall C 160 aircraft during in-flight lightning strikes. The measurements allowed a more precise determination of the internal magnetic field behind a composite panel located on the forward fuselage.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recursion relations for three-dimensional scalar addition theorem
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Efficient recursion relations for the elements of the translation matrix are derived. These recursion relations are a lot more efficient than the previous ones. It is noted that the efficient evaluation of the addition theorem is important in a number of scattering applications, especially in fast recursive algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A resistive edge treated Gregorian subreflector for a dual chamber compact range measurement system
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The performance of a dual-chamber compact range measurement system with a resistive edge treated Gregorian subreflector was studied. It was shown that the resistive edge treated Gregorian subreflector can provide a good-quality target zone. For the best performance, the resistive cards should be as large as possible and should have zero resistance near the basic subreflector edges. For nonzero resistance near the edges, the basic subreflector should be made a little larger. Thus, one may wish to use a somewhat smaller resistive card.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering from a randomly rough half-plane
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The scattering and diffraction of a plane wave by a randomly rough half-plane are investigated. Such a nonplane boundary problem is related to the degradation of an antenna due to the random distortion of the reflector and the scattering and diffraction by rough walls. The present formulation is a combination of three techniques: the small perturbation, the Wiener-Hopf method, and a group-theoretic consideration for determining the form of the scattered wave. Using the shift invariant property of the homogeneous random plane, the D/sup a/-Fourier transform which converts the scattered wave into a homogeneous random function of x with a complex variable is defined. Assuming a slightly rough case, such a homogeneous random function is expanded into a perturbation series. The first-order wave field is then obtained by the Wiener-Hopf technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Who needs electromagnetism? (or an exercise in masochism in UK universities)
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: The author presents his perceptions on how EM is being taught in UK universities and specifically on where use is being made of some form of computer-aided instruction. It is concluded that the overriding reasons why EM software does not feature strongly in UK degree programs are the lack of resources and the heavy loading on staff. The problem is certainly not confined to EM courses but is probably more acute there because there is no doubt that this subject, probably more than any other, can benefit from the processing power and exceptional graphics now available in the desk-top computer. However, this requires a significant investment of academic staff time to implement, and this is a commodity in short supply at present.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of biconical microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: Antennas and Propagation Society Symposium 1991 Digest
abstract: Characteristics of biconical microstrip antennas asymmetrically excited by a coaxial probe feed are studied. The antenna consists of a conducting cone cap on a grounded cone separated by an electrically thin dielectric. A study of the theta -dependent eigenvalues nu of the spherical wave functions in the omega direction has shown that there is a unique nontrivial eigenvalue for each TE (transverse electric) mode, and for the TM (transverse magnetic) modes all eigenvalues are trivial solutions. Their input impedance, bandwidth, and radiation patterns for different grounded cone angles are presented. The analysis of the conical microstrip antenna, the special case of these antennas, where the grounded core becomes a plane, predicts that their bandwidth is wider than that of similar-size planar circular disc antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
